questions.ask: What is your year of birth?
What is the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
What is your full date of birth?

intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period ("after payday") instead of an exact day.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

assumptions: Currency is euros. The API says EUR, and brief rule 10 says to speak amounts in euros.
The API gives amounts in euro cents and create_promise also takes cents, so amount_scale is 100 and promise_scale is null.
Workdays are Monday to Saturday, because Saturday is a full business day. Sunday and the holidays 2026-11-21, 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-25 are not business days.
The brief does not say how to read 'next <weekday>', so the default following_week is used.

Callback days are today or either of the next two business days, so days is ['today', 'within_business_days:2'] and business_days_only is true. Hours are 09:00-18:00 Monday to Friday and 09:00-13:00 Saturday, with no callbacks on Sunday.

Callback max_asks is 2. If the person's first time is outside the rules, the agent proposes one valid time. If they refuse it, the call closes as no_callback (rule 4). The tp_outside_window line assumes the engine fills {date} and {time} with the proposed slot.

Rule 2 says to ask once more if the answer is unclear, so confirm.max_asks is 2. The brief gives full_name and salutation instead of first name, last name and title, so both are declared as call variables.
Identity: one wrong answer is forgiven and the second ends the check, counted over the whole check. So max_wrong is 2 and max_wrong_per_question is null. The API summary agrees.

Verify fields come from the API enum: birth_year (four digits), customer_code (five characters, capital letters, no spaces) and birth_date (DD.MM.YYYY = %d.%m.%Y). A date said only as numbers is read day, month, year.

In the verify response, verified maps to 'correct' and all_verified to 'identity_passed'. The API has no 'wrong answers left' field and no hint field. Its 'wrong_answers' field counts wrong answers so far and is not a remaining count, so left and hint are left empty and the engine counts against max_wrong. A wrongly formatted answer returns ok=false and is not counted.
The brief does not say whether asking about the purpose counts as declining the questions, so the default (true) is kept.
get_account returns a single 'account' object, not an array. list_field is set to 'account', id_field to product_id and type_field to product_kind.

Floors depend on the product. The card floor is statement_minimum_cents (floor_field). The overdraft floor is 20% of amount_due_cents rounded up to the next whole euro (floor_pct 20, floor_round up_unit). floor_pct applies only to the overdraft, which has no floor_field. Credit and overdraft limits are never used.

Middle band deadline: the 8th business day after today for a card and the 5th for an overdraft (deadline_by_type). Late band: the later of the last business day of the month and the 3rd business day after today. Early band: the last business day of next week, which is Saturday unless that is a holiday.

Recoveries band (61 or more days): no proposal and no promise. The spec format has no event key for this, so an extra 'recoveries' event was added (handed_over / recoveries, queue recoveries) and linked through bands_outside. A recoveries_line was added for the handover sentence.

The brief gives no rule for days_overdue below 1. Because only one product is ever called about and it is overdue, values outside the three bands are treated as the recoveries band through bands_outside.

Ladder: attempt 1 is the full amount on the 2nd business day after today, or the floor if the customer has already said the full amount is too much (full_or_floor). Attempt 2 is the floor on the deadline, for the middle and late bands only, which is enforced by the attempts count.

Rule 17 says to offer the floor once when the full amount is too much, and rule 20 makes attempt 1 the floor on the 2nd business day in that case. So too_much_floor is 'attempt_1': the single floor offer is attempt 1, on attempt 1's date, and it uses that attempt.

Rule 13: a Sunday or holiday rolls back to the previous business day (deadline_adjust previous_business_day), or forward if that day is before today. Rule 14: refusing the deadline counts as a refusal.
The first ask is the full amount today (rule 19).

Hardship (rule 28): one sentence of sympathy, add_note with reason vulnerable, then a transfer to the 'care' queue, closing as handed_over / vulnerable. The brief transfers directly and makes no offer, so the hardship line announces the transfer.
Notes are written only under rules 24, 26, 27 and 28 (system_fault, paid_claim, disputed, vulnerable). notes.enabled is false, and refusals get no note.
add_note in the API has no product id field. The required n_product slot is mapped to the optional free-text field 'text', which then carries the product id. reason is mapped to n_reason.

The brief does not say whether to give the customer a further turn after a recorded promise, so the default ask_anything_else true is kept. The required sentence after recording is 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' (sms_line).
The brief gives no rule for changing a recorded promise, so the agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
The opening says 'We record this call' (active voice) to meet the brief's requirement to say the call is recorded.
Every tool's success flag is 'ok' = true, as given in the API responses.
There is only one product per call, so the multi-product settings keep their defaults.
